claims.claim: **Common: found in more than a third of healthy children.** A well-appearing child usually needs observation and reassurance, without investigation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lymphadenopathy means abnormally enlarged head and neck nodes, usually over 1 cm.** Viral URTI is the commonest cause, and reactive nodes can remain for weeks or even months.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask about** travel and possible TB exposure, animals such as cats, immunisation status, dental disease, response to antibiotics, and features of deep neck infection (e.g. trismus, muffled voice).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Acute bacterial lymphadenitis:** usually unilateral, anterior neck, with fever; firm and tender with overlying erythema; may be fluctuant. Causes: *S. aureus*, group B strep (neonates), group A strep, anaerobes with dental disease.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Rarely linked to a deep neck infection such as retropharyngeal abscess.** Kawasaki disease can present with unilateral tender cervical nodes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Subacute (2–6 weeks): usually viral. Chronic (over 6 weeks): several possible causes.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider malignancy if nodes are prolonged, painless and firm**, especially with weight loss, night sweats, easy bruising, hepatosplenomegaly or a mediastinal mass.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **TB:** non-tender nodes, exposure history, fever, malaise, weight loss. **Atypical mycobacteria:** indolent, chronic unilateral nodes with a violaceous hue, usually under 5 years.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cat scratch disease:** usually tender nodes in the axilla. **Head and neck eczema** can cause prominent posterior cervical nodes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If investigating:** TB skin test or QuantiFERON if TB is suspected; chest X-ray if malignancy is suspected; neck ultrasound; CT or MRI may be needed before surgery. **Excisional biopsy is the gold standard; FNA is less helpful.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most cases are self-limited and need no treatment.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bacterial lymphadenitis (unilateral, tender, fluctuant), well child: cefalexin 20 mg/kg (max 750 mg) orally tds for 7 days, reviewed at 48 hours.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unwell, or failed oral treatment: IV cefazolin 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) every 8 hours.** Follow local susceptibility patterns.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A fluctuant node not responding to IV antibiotics: consult surgeons about incision and drainage.** ⚠️ **Suspected mycobacterial infection: excise the whole node**, since incision and drainage may leave a sinus.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team for:** a neonate, an unwell child, nodes persisting despite oral antibiotics, or features of systemic disease (Kawasaki, malignancy, rheumatological).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer** a child needing care beyond the hospital's comfort level.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cervical_lymphadenopathy/, retrieved 2026-09-23
